The **Cancer Distribution** among acute surgical patients provides a critical epidemiological overview of cancer prevalence within the Danish healthcare system, specifically detailing the types and frequencies of cancer diagnoses found in patients undergoing acute surgery. This data is tracked and reported by the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (Acute Surgery Database) as part of the broader quality assurance efforts by the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] (Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme) [^src1]. Understanding this distribution is vital for resource allocation, surgical planning, and oncological follow-up in emergency and acute care settings.

Nationally, the data reveals that the vast majority of acute surgical patients do not have a cancer diagnosis. Out of 3,151 operated patients in Denmark, 2,935 (93.15%) had no cancer diagnosis [^src1]. Among those who did, gastrointestinal cancers were the most prevalent, affecting 159 patients (5.05%), followed by other types of cancer in 42 patients (1.33%), and gynecological cancers in 15 patients (0.48%) [^src1].

When examining the [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]] (Capital Region), the database recorded 1,095 operated patients [^src1]. The regional breakdown highlights the specific patient volumes and cancer distributions across its major hospitals. [[herlev-og-gentofte-hospital|Herlev og Gentofte Hospital]] handled the highest volume in this dataset with 306 operated patients, including 19 with gastrointestinal cancers and 4 with other cancers [^src1]. [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] followed with 256 patients (15 gastrointestinal, 4 other cancers) [^src1], and [[bispebjerg-og-frederiksberg-hospitaler|Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospitaler]] with 231 patients (14 gastrointestinal, 4 other cancers) [^src1]. [[hospitalerne-i-nordsjaelland|Hospitalerne i Nordsjælland]] reported 214 operated patients, with an even split of 4 gastrointestinal and 4 other cancer cases [^src1]. [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] had 58 operated patients in this specific cohort, with 3 cases of other cancers and no reported gastrointestinal or gynecological cancers [^src1]. Finally, [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] recorded 30 operated patients, none of whom had a cancer diagnosis [^src1].

This granular, hospital-level distribution underscores the varying oncological burdens faced by different acute surgical departments across the Capital Region, informing both regional health policies and clinical quality development.
